A1.justification: The PDFs clearly describe the same work, and their main text and displays are readable. However, v1's Appendix on page 12 refers to separate, unsupplied supplementary material containing technical details and transfer analyses. V2 includes Appendices A–D, limiting reliable comparison of material previously relegated to v1's missing supplement.

before.justification: V1 reports original diffusion attribution experiments, semantic attribution results, counterfactual retraining, and pruning measurements in Sections 3 and 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification, language-modeling, diffusion, and semantic attribution results, with further empirical analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: V1's normalized top-k minus bottom-k objective (Eq. 7) becomes a normalized top-k-only objective in v2 (Eq. 6). The previous objective becomes an ablation in Appendix C.3. This changes the central learning criterion while retaining parameter-group weighting. V1's attribution-pruning extension is also removed.

E1.justification: V2 expands beyond diffusion to ImageNet classification and mislabeled-data detection, plus WikiText-103 language modeling and training-proponent evaluation. The four diffusion datasets—CIFAR-2, ArtBench-2, Naruto, and SB-Pokemon—and the semantic attribution task are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated LoGRA and EKFAC comparators for language modeling (Tables 2 and 4), including an explicitly described LoGRA-feature/EKFAC-kernel implementation, and a random tail-patch control. The five diffusion comparators remain; JTRAK and DTRAK correspond to v1's JourneyTRAK and D-TRAK.

E3.justification: V2 introduces ImageNet evaluation with 10% label corruption and AUC, and GPT-2 tail-patch updates using 128 proponents. V1's 64-query, top-20%-removal retraining protocol and pruning/projection sweeps disappear. Some new settings conflict internally: ImageNet LDS uses 500 queries in Section 5.1.1 versus 1,000 in B.2.1, while tail-patch measures relative probability increase in Section 5.1.2 versus log-probability change in B.2.3.

E4.justification: The analysis scope changes substantially: v1's counterfactual retraining and pruning analyses disappear, while v2 presents k sensitivity, alternative-loss ablations, and parameter-signal consistency analyses (Appendices C.1–C.3). Tables 10–11 document transfer tests already mentioned in v1; their novelty cannot be established without its missing supplement.

E5.justification: V1's tables contain point estimates, and its checklist states that multiple trials were conducted without reporting table error bars. V2 reports 95% confidence-interval half-widths for LDS and tail-patch comparisons and adds Figure 1 error bars calculated over 1,000 samples. This expands uncertainty reporting without establishing increased repeated-run counts; the CI estimation procedure remains unspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds ImageNet and WikiText-103 results and substantially revises diffusion LDS values. For example, CIFAR-2 TRAK baseline/weighted scores change from 37.5/46.3 in v1 Table 1 to 8.51/10.59 in v2 Table 5. Matched settings are not established, so this is not a controlled performance regression. V1 Table 4's fine-grained recall values remain unchanged in v2 Table 6.

T1.justification: V1 provides attribution formulas but declares no theoretical results. V2 Appendix A introduces a signal-plus-noise model, independence and sparsity assumptions, derives optimal weights proportional to signal sensitivity divided by noise variance, and links its loss to SNR maximization. The latter argument does not justify discarding noise after selecting examples by their noisy top-k scores.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and conclusion broaden the claimed demonstrated applicability from diffusion-focused attribution to classification, language modeling, and diffusion. The conclusion newly characterizes the framework as SNR-grounded and drops the pruning contribution. Label-free parameter weighting and fine-grained semantic attribution remain central claims.

C2.justification: V2 develops SNR and noise-filtering interpretations and emphasizes coarse layer-wise weighting and dataset-dependent k sensitivity as limitations. Its transfer discussion adds substantive interpretations, but C.4 overstates Table 10: ArtBench-trained weights do not outperform Naruto-trained weights for TracIn (13.48 versus 13.59) or JTRAK (14.36 versus 14.56).

D1.justification: V2 documents softmax weighting, optimization schedules, projection dimensions, dataset generation, and pseudocode in Appendix B. However, v1 explicitly places implementation details in its unavailable supplement, preventing a reliable judgment of how much is newly disclosed, revised, or relocated. Visible changes include details for the added models and removal of v1's future code/data-release commitment.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around influence functions, Hessian approximations, and existing parameter-subset selection. It adds an LLM-attribution discussion covering Grosse et al., LoGRA, and TrackStar, plus additional parameter-specialization references. This revises the diffusion-centered account of prior work while retaining the claim of explicitly addressing parameter heterogeneity.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized by task domain, dataset descriptions move to Appendix B.1, and the separate fine-grained-method subsection is folded into Section 4.2. V1's appendix notice and NeurIPS checklist are replaced by structured appendices; the title and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds four main classification/language tables, redesigns the diffusion comparison table, and removes the counterfactual and pruning tables. Figures 1 and 3 are redrawn; Figure 1 changes to percentage axes, a smoothing window of seven instead of five, and error bars. Dataset illustrations, consistency heatmaps, appendix tables, and a different document template further change presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 directly tests applicability beyond diffusion, which v1 left to future work, and Table 9 evaluates the revised objective against the previous loss and alternatives. Main-table confidence intervals also improve assessment of the evidence. These support a limited net gain, tempered by removal of counterfactual/pruning evidence, conflicting sample counts and tail-patch definitions, and overstatements in the SNR and transfer arguments. V1's missing supplement limits conclusions about improved reproducibility and newly added appendix analyses.
